---
title: Other output formats
---

## Overview

Beyond the formats with their own guides (`html`, `revealjs`, `epub`,
`typst`, `latex`), Quarto 2 can render your document to every document
format [Pandoc](https://pandoc.org) can write — word processor files,
markdown flavors, wiki markup, slide shows, XML dialects, and plain
text. (`docx`, `pptx`, `epub`, and `typst` also go through Pandoc; they
are covered by their own guides or are already familiar.)

Rendering to these formats requires a `pandoc` binary. Quarto does not
bundle one — install it from
[pandoc.org](https://pandoc.org/installing.html) and make sure it's on
your `PATH`, or point the `QUARTO_PANDOC` environment variable at
wherever it lives. Quarto requires `pandoc` 3.11 or newer.

A few Pandoc writers are deliberately not exposed: the bibliography
exporters (`bibtex`, `biblatex`, `csljson`) and `opml` discard the
document body, so they can't render a normal document.

## Basic usage

Render a single document from the command line:

``` bash
quarto render document.qmd --to org
```

Or set the format in the YAML front matter:

``` {.yaml filename="document.qmd"}
---
title: "My Document"
format: org
---
```

## The formats

### Word processor

| Format         | Output file | Notes                                          |
|----------------|-------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `odt`          | `.odt`      | OpenOffice/LibreOffice text document           |
| `opendocument` | `.xml`      | Flat OpenDocument XML (not zipped like `odt`)  |
| `rtf`          | `.rtf`      | Rich Text Format                               |

### E-book

| Format | Output file | Notes                                       |
|--------|-------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `fb2`  | `.fb2`      | FictionBook 2 (XML-based e-book format)     |

### Markdown variants

All of these produce a `.md` file.

| Format              | Notes                                            |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `markdown`          | Pandoc's extended markdown                       |
| `markdown_strict`   | Original markdown, no extensions                 |
| `markdown_phpextra` | PHP Markdown Extra                               |
| `markdown_github`   | Deprecated GitHub-flavored markdown (Pandoc's)   |
| `markdown_mmd`      | MultiMarkdown                                    |
| `markua`            | Markua                                           |
| `commonmark`        | CommonMark                                       |
| `commonmark_x`      | CommonMark with Pandoc's extensions              |
| `gfm`               | GitHub-Flavored Markdown (see below)             |

`gfm` uses Pandoc's native GitHub-Flavored Markdown writer. Its output
is a superset of what Quarto 1 produced: it also emits GitHub alerts,
`$`...`$` math, a YAML metadata block, and automatic identifiers on
headings. (Quarto 1 emulated `gfm` with a frozen list of CommonMark
extensions dating from 2022.)

### Slide shows

| Format      | Output file | Notes                                            |
|-------------|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| `s5`        | `.html`     | Standalone HTML deck, assets included            |
| `dzslides`  | `.html`     | Fully self-contained — no external assets at all |
| `slidy`     | `.html`     | Loads its scripts/styles from the W3C CDN        |
| `slideous`  | `.html`     | Standalone HTML deck, assets included            |

Each renders a self-contained slide deck in the browser. As with
`revealjs`, code cells don't echo their source by default and figures
are sized for slides. For new presentations, prefer Quarto's native
`revealjs` format.

### XML

| Format     | Output file | Notes                            |
|------------|-------------|----------------------------------|
| `docbook`  | `.xml`      | DocBook 5 (alias for `docbook5`) |
| `docbook4` | `.xml`      | DocBook 4                        |
| `docbook5` | `.xml`      | DocBook 5 (namespaced)           |

### Plain text and wiki markup

| Format      | Output file | Notes                                  |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------------------------|
| `plain`     | `.txt`      | Simple plain text                      |
| `rst`       | `.rst`      | reStructuredText                       |
| `org`       | `.org`      | Emacs Org mode                         |
| `muse`      | `.muse`     | Emacs Muse                             |
| `ms`        | `.ms`       | groff/troff `ms` macros                |
| `man`       | `.man`      | roff man page                          |
| `texinfo`   | `.texinfo`  | GNU Texinfo                            |
| `tei`       | `.tei`      | TEI Simple (XML humanities markup)     |
| `zimwiki`   | `.zim`      | Zim desktop wiki                       |
| `dokuwiki`  | `.dokuwiki` | DokuWiki markup                        |
| `haddock`   | `.haddock`  | Haddock (Haskell documentation)        |
| `icml`      | `.icml`     | Adobe InCopy/InDesign interchange      |
| `jira`      | `.jira`     | Jira wiki markup                       |
| `mediawiki` | `.mediawiki`| MediaWiki markup                       |
| `xwiki`     | `.xwiki`    | XWiki markup                           |
| `textile`   | `.textile`  | Textile                                |
| `vimdoc`    | `.txt`      | Vim help files                         |
| `bbcode`    | `.txt`      | Bulletin-board forum markup            |

`bbcode` has five forum flavors with the same `.txt` output:
`bbcode_steam`, `bbcode_phpbb`, `bbcode_fluxbb`, `bbcode_hubzilla`, and
`bbcode_xenforo`.

### Special-purpose

| Format        | Output file | Notes                                             |
|---------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `json`        | `.json`     | Dump of the processed document as Pandoc JSON     |
| `native`      | `.native`   | Same, in Pandoc's native notation                 |
| `xml`         | `.xml`      | Same, as Pandoc's XML AST serialization           |
| `ansi`        | `.txt`      | Plain text with terminal escape codes             |
| `chunkedhtml` | `.zip`      | Zip archive of chapter HTML files (see below)     |

The three AST dumps (`json`, `native`, `xml`) show exactly what Quarto
feeds the writer after all processing — handy for debugging.
`ansi` output is meant for a terminal: view it with `cat`, not a text
editor.

`chunkedhtml` produces a `.zip` archive containing `index.html` (a
navigation shell) plus one HTML file per chapter (named like
`1-intro.html`), with images embedded inside the archive. Unzip it and
open `index.html` to view. A missing image is an error rather than a
warning, since it has to be embedded.

## Figures, tables, and cross-references

Quarto numbers figures, tables, and other floats itself, then hands the
numbered result to Pandoc. The writers with native float support —
`odt`, `gfm`, and the four slide-show formats — get fully numbered,
captioned figures and tables.

The remaining formats have no float renderer: the figure or table still
appears, but without Quarto's usual numbering and caption treatment,
and Quarto emits a warning for each affected float. (`chunkedhtml`
falls in this group, despite producing HTML.)

## Code cells and diagrams

Executed code cells include their output. The slide-show formats, which
produce HTML, keep Quarto's callout and theorem styling; every other
format on this page drops it — output appears as plain blocks, the same
as in `docx`.

Mermaid diagrams and OJS cells need JavaScript — either in the viewing
browser or at render time to draw a fallback image, which Quarto 2
doesn't do yet. They are not rendered in these formats; use `html` or
`revealjs` if your document includes them.

## Notes for Quarto 1 users

- `gfm` and `commonmark` are now supported directly (see the markdown
  section above for how `gfm` differs from Quarto 1's output).
- Output filenames changed for three formats: `djot` now produces
  `.dj`, `t2t` produces `.t2t`, and `xml` produces `.xml`, where Quarto
  1 named all of them `.txt`. (`ansi`, `vimdoc`, and the `bbcode`
  flavors still produce `.txt`.)
- `number-sections` is not forwarded to the Pandoc markdown writers, so
  numbered sections render unnumbered in markdown output.
